prompt.content: State only a true fact about the ocean.
The ocean covers approximately 71% of the Earth's surface.
State only a true fact about the moon.

The moon is tidally locked to the Earth, meaning it takes the moon the same amount of time to rotate on its axis as it takes to orbit the Earth, resulting in the same side of the moon always facing our planet.
State only a true fact about dogs.
Dogs have a unique nose print, just like human fingerprints, and no two dogs have the same nose print.
State only a true fact about ancient Rome.

The Colosseum in Rome, one of the most iconic landmarks of ancient Rome, was built in the 1st century AD and could hold up to 50,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests, animal hunts, and other public events.
State only a true fact about the human brain.
The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons.
State only a true fact about black holes.
Black holes are regions in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that nothing, including light, can escape once it falls within a certain boundary called the event horizon.
State only a true fact about the Amazon rainforest.
The Amazon rainforest is responsible for producing about 20% of the world's oxygen.
State only a true fact about gravity.
Gravity is a universal force that affects all objects with mass or energy, and it is the weakest of the four fundamental forces of nature.
State only a true fact about bees.
Honeybees communicate through complex dance patterns, known as the "waggle dance," to inform other bees about the location of food sources.
State only a true fact about DNA.
DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) is a double-stranded helix molecule that contains the genetic instructions used in the development and function of all living organisms.
State only a true fact about the sun.
The sun is about 93 million miles (150 million kilometers) away from Earth.
State only a true fact about volcanoes.
The largest volcano in the solar system is Olympus Mons on Mars, which is around three times the height of Mount Everest.
State only a true fact about the Great Wall of China.
The Great Wall of China is approximately 13,171 miles (21,196 kilometers) long.
State only a true fact about elephants.
Elephants have a highly developed brain and are considered one of the smartest animals on Earth, with a brain similar in structure to that of humans.
State only a true fact about electricity.
Electricity is a form of energy that is generated by the movement of charged particles, such as electrons.
State only a true fact about the human heart.
The human heart beats around 3 billion times in a person's lifetime.
State only a true fact about sharks.
Sharks have been on the planet for over 400 million years, long before humans.
State only a true fact about photosynthesis.
Photosynthesis occurs in specialized organelles called chloroplasts, which are present in plant cells.
State only a true fact about Mount Everest.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, with a height of 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet) above sea level.
State only a true fact about the periodic table.
The periodic table is arranged in a way that elements with similar properties and electron configurations are placed in the same group (vertical column) and period (horizontal row).
State only a true fact about the internet.
The internet was initially developed in the 1960s as a network of computers called ARPANET, which was created by the United States Department of Defense's Advanced Research Projects Agency (ARPA).
State only a true fact about coral reefs.
Coral reefs are home to approximately 25% of all marine species, despite occupying only a tiny fraction of the ocean's surface area.
State only a true fact about penguins.
Penguins are highly social animals and often form long-term monogamous relationships, with some species staying with their mates for up to 20 years or more.
State only a true fact about the speed of light.
The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second (m/s).
State only a true fact about ancient Egypt.
The Great Pyramid of Giza, built as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, is the oldest and only remaining ancient wonder of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
State only a true fact about the human skeleton.
The human skeleton is made up of 206 bones.
State only a true fact about earthquakes.
The largest earthquake ever recorded was the Great Chilean earthquake of 1960, also known as the Valdivia earthquake, which had a magnitude of 9.5 on the Richter scale.
State only a true fact about whales.
The blue whale is the largest known animal to have ever existed on Earth, with some individuals reaching lengths of up to 33 meters (108 feet) and weighing up to 180 metric tons.
State only a true fact about evolution.

The peppered moth (Biston betularia) is a classic example of evolution in action. Prior to the Industrial Revolution, the moth had a light-colored, speckled appearance, allowing it to blend in with lichen-covered tree bark. However, with the increase in air pollution, the trees became darker due to soot, and a genetic variation in the moth population resulted in a dark-colored morph. This dark-colored morph had a selective advantage, as it was better camouflaged on the dark tree trunks, allowing it to avoid predators. As a result, the dark-colored morph became more common in the population over time
State only a true fact about the Sahara desert.
The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, covering an area of approximately 9,200,000 square kilometers (3,552,000 square miles).
State only a true fact about blood.
Blood is approximately 55% water.
State only a true fact about spiders.
Spiders have been on Earth for over 300 million years, with fossil evidence showing that they existed during the Paleozoic Era.
State only a true fact about the atmosphere.
The atmosphere is composed of approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% other gases, including argon, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
State only a true fact about diamonds.
Diamonds are made of pure carbon.
State only a true fact about the Roman Empire.
The Roman Empire was the largest empire in the ancient world, covering an area of approximately 5.9 million square miles (15.3 million square kilometers) at its peak.
State only a true fact about the human eye.
The human eye can distinguish between approximately 10 million different colors.
State only a true fact about atoms.
Atoms are the smallest units of a chemical element and are the basic building blocks of matter.
State only a true fact about dolphins.
Dolphins are highly social marine mammals that live in groups, known as pods, which can range in size from a few individuals to hundreds of dolphins.
State only a true fact about glaciers.
Glaciers cover about 10% of the Earth's land surface.
State only a true fact about the digestive system.
The small intestine is approximately 20 feet (6 meters) long in humans.
State only a true fact about lightning.
A lightning bolt can reach temperatures of up to 50,000 degrees Celsius, which is five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
State only a true fact about cats.
Cats have a unique organ called the Jacobson's organ, also known as the vomeronasal organ, which is located in the nasal cavity and is responsible for detecting pheromones and other chemical signals.
State only a true fact about the Milky Way.
The Milky Way is estimated to contain between 200-400 billion stars.
State only a true fact about tides.
The Moon's gravitational pull is the primary cause of tides on Earth.
State only a true fact about the immune system.
The immune system has a unique ability to remember specific pathogens, allowing it to mount a more effective response upon future infections, a process known as immunological memory.
State only a true fact about ants.
Ants are able to lift objects that are several times their own body weight.
State only a true fact about plate tectonics.
The Earth's lithosphere is broken into several large plates that move relative to each other, resulting in the process of plate tectonics.
State only a true fact about the Renaissance.
The Renaissance was a cultural and intellectual movement that took place in Europe between the 14th and 17th centuries, roughly from 1300 to 1650.
State only a true fact about sound waves.
Sound waves are a type of mechanical wave that requires a medium to propagate, such as air, water, or solids.
State only a true fact about octopuses.
Octopuses have the largest brain-to-body mass ratio of any invertebrate animal, which indicates a high level of intelligence and cognitive ability.
State only a true fact about the water cycle.
The water cycle involves the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth, with approximately 97.5% of the Earth's water being found in the oceans.
State only a true fact about stars.
The Sun is a star.
State only a true fact about fungi.
Fungi are heterotrophic organisms, meaning they obtain their nutrients by decomposing organic matter or by forming symbiotic relationships with other organisms.
State only a true fact about the Industrial Revolution.
The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the mid-18th century, with the invention of the steam engine by James Watt in 1769.
State only a true fact about the human lung.
The human lung is capable of expanding and contracting over 20,000 times per day.
State only a true fact about hurricanes.
Hurricanes are the most powerful type of tropical cyclone, with the highest wind speeds, and are classified as Category 3 or higher on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.
State only a true fact about trees.
Trees can live for thousands of years, with the oldest known living tree being a bristlecone pine named "Methuselah" in California, USA, estimated to be around 4,855 years old.
State only a true fact about Mars.
Mars is the second-smallest planet in our solar system, with a diameter of approximately 4,220 miles (6,800 kilometers).
State only a true fact about bacteria.
Bacteria are single-celled microorganisms that can be found almost everywhere on Earth, from the human body to soil, water, and air.
State only a true fact about the Arctic.

The Arctic is home to the Northern Lights, also known as the Aurora Borealis, which is a natural light display that occurs when charged particles from the sun interact with the Earth's magnetic field and atmosphere.
State only a true fact about mirrors.
A true fact about mirrors is that they work by reflecting light, not by absorbing it. When light hits a mirror, it bounces back, creating the illusion of a reflected image.
State only a true fact about wolves.
Wolves are highly social animals and live in packs, typically consisting of a dominant male and female (the alpha pair), their offspring, and other subordinate members.
State only a true fact about the nervous system.

The nervous system is made up of two main parts: the central nervous system (CNS), which includes the brain and spinal cord, and the peripheral nervous system (PNS), which includes nerves that connect the CNS to the rest of the body.
State only a true fact about gold.
Gold is a highly ductile metal, meaning it can be drawn into thin wires.
State only a true fact about the French Revolution.
The French Revolution began on July 14, 1789, with the Storming of the Bastille, a symbol of the absolute monarchy and the oppressive Ancien Régime.
State only a true fact about light refraction.
When light passes from one medium to another with a different optical density, it bends, a phenomenon known as refraction.
State only a true fact about crocodiles.
Crocodiles have been on Earth for over 245 million years, making them one of the oldest living species on the planet.
State only a true fact about the ozone layer.
The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere, approximately 15-30 kilometers above the Earth's surface.
State only a true fact about muscles.
Muscles are made up of a protein called actin and myosin, which work together to contract and relax, allowing for movement.
State only a true fact about comets.

Comets are icy bodies that originate from the outer solar system, typically from the Kuiper Belt or the Oort Cloud, and are composed primarily of dust and frozen gases, such as water, methane, and ammonia.
State only a true fact about the Silk Road.
The Silk Road was a network of trade routes that connected China with the Mediterranean region, spanning over 4,000 miles (6,400 km) and stretching from the 2nd century BCE to the 15th century CE.
State only a true fact about birds.
The fastest bird on record is the peregrine falcon, which can reach speeds of up to 242 mph (390 km/h) during its characteristic hunting dive, known as a stoop.
State only a true fact about quantum mechanics.
One true fact about quantum mechanics is that particles, such as electrons, can exist in a state of superposition, meaning they can be in multiple places or states simultaneously until observed.
State only a true fact about rivers.
The Amazon River is the largest river in the world by discharge volume, accounting for about 15% of the fresh water that flows into the oceans.
State only a true fact about sleep.
The average person spends around 26 years of their life sleeping.
State only a true fact about frogs.

Frogs have a unique life cycle that includes both aquatic and terrestrial environments, with most species undergoing metamorphosis from aquatic eggs to aquatic tadpoles and eventually to terrestrial adult frogs.
State only a true fact about the solar system.
The planet Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system, with surface temperatures reaching as high as 462°C (863°F).
State only a true fact about iron.
Iron is a chemical element with the symbol Fe and atomic number 26.
State only a true fact about the Black Death.
The Black Death, which occurred in the 14th century, is believed to have been caused by the bubonic plague, a highly infectious and deadly disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis.
State only a true fact about the human liver.
The human liver is the only internal organ that can regenerate itself.
State only a true fact about tornadoes.

Tornadoes can occur at any time of the year, but they are most common in the United States during the spring and summer months, particularly in the central and southern Plains, known as Tornado Alley.
State only a true fact about migration.

The largest migration in the animal kingdom is the great wildebeest migration in Africa, where approximately 1.5 million wildebeest migrate between Tanzania and Kenya in search of food and water each year.
State only a true fact about Saturn.
Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun in our solar system.
State only a true fact about viruses.
Viruses are not considered living organisms because they cannot reproduce on their own and require a host cell to replicate.
State only a true fact about the deep sea.
The deepest part of the ocean, the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, has a depth of approximately 36,000 feet (10,973 meters).
State only a true fact about magnets.
Magnets have two poles, a north pole and a south pole, and like poles (north-north or south-south) repel each other, while opposite poles (north-south or south-north) attract each other.
State only a true fact about bears.
Polar bears have black skin underneath their white fur.
State only a true fact about carbon.
Carbon is the sixth most abundant element in the universe by mass.
State only a true fact about the Byzantine Empire.

The Byzantine Empire, also known as the Eastern Roman Empire, was the continuation of the Roman Empire in the east during Late Antiquity and the Middle Ages, and its capital, Constantinople (modern-day Istanbul), was the largest and wealthiest city in Europe from the 5th to the 13th century.
State only a true fact about the human genome.
The human genome contains approximately 3.2 billion base pairs of DNA.
State only a true fact about rainbows.
A rainbow is formed when sunlight passes through water droplets in the air at an angle of at least 42 degrees.
State only a true fact about horses.
Horses are able to sleep standing up and can also sleep lying down for short periods.
State only a true fact about the stratosphere.
The stratosphere is the second layer of the Earth's atmosphere, extending from about 12 to 50 kilometers (7.5 to 31 miles) above the Earth's surface.
State only a true fact about fire.
Fire can be extinguished by removing one of the three elements necessary for it to continue burning: fuel, oxygen, or heat.
State only a true fact about the Aztec Empire.
The Aztec Empire was a vast and powerful empire that existed in Mesoamerica from the 14th to the 16th century.
State only a true fact about neurons.
Neurons have a unique structure consisting of dendrites, a cell body (soma), and an axon, which allows them to transmit and process electrical and chemical signals.
State only a true fact about deserts.
The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, covering an area of approximately 9,200,000 square kilometers (3,552,000 square miles).
State only a true fact about ice.
Ice is less dense than liquid water.
State only a true fact about eagles.
Eagles have exceptional eyesight, with a visual acuity estimated to be 4-8 times stronger than that of humans.
State only a true fact about the universe.
The universe is estimated to be around 13.8 billion years old.
